[F13] (refund.v1 - 5.1) Where an event is canceled by the promoter, the ticket price and the booking fee are both refunded in full, automatically, within ten business days. No request is required.
[F14] (refund.v1 - 5.2) Where an event is rescheduled by the promoter, tickets remain valid for the new date. A holder who cannot attend the new date may request a full refund of the ticket price and the booking fee within 14 days of the reschedule being announced.

# Established facts

### policy_clauses
[F1] (refund.v1 - 1.1) This policy governs refunds requested by the ticket holder. Refunds arising from an event being canceled or rescheduled by the promoter are governed by section 5 and are not subject to the windows in section 2.
[F2] (refund.v1 - 1.2) Every ticket is sold with a booking fee. The booking fee is stated separately at checkout.
[F3] (refund.v1 - 2.1) A full refund of the ticket price is available where the request is made more than 14 days before the scheduled door time.
[F4] (refund.v1 - 2.2) Where the request is made between 14 days and 72 hours before the scheduled door time, 50% of the ticket price is refundable.
[F5] (refund.v1 - 2.3) No refund of the ticket price is available where the request is made within 72 hours of the scheduled door time.
[F6] (refund.v1 - 2.4) The booking fee is non-refundable under this section, including where a full refund of the ticket price is due.
[F7] (refund.v1 - 3.1) A refund is issued to the original payment method. Where the original method is no longer valid, the refund is held until the account holder supplies a replacement.
[F8] (refund.v1 - 3.2) Card refunds are submitted to Cardinal Pay within one business day and reach the cardholder's statement within five business days of submission.
[F9] (refund.v1 - 3.3) Partial refunds against a split-tender payment are submitted to each instrument in the proportion originally charged.
[F10] (refund.v1 - 4.1) A refund cannot be issued against a booking whose tickets have been transferred to another named holder. The transfer must be reversed by the current holder before a refund can be requested.
[F11] (refund.v1 - 4.2) A booking that has been exchanged retains the refund window of the *original* purchase, not of the event it was exchanged into.
[F12] (refund.v1 - 4.3) Where any ticket on a booking has been scanned at the venue, no ticket on that booking is refundable.
[F13] (refund.v1 - 5.1) Where an event is canceled by the promoter, the ticket price and the booking fee are both refunded in full, automatically, within ten business days. No request is required.
[F14] (refund.v1 - 5.2) Where an event is rescheduled by the promoter, tickets remain valid for the new date. A holder who cannot attend the new date may request a full refund of the ticket price and the booking fee within 14 days of the reschedule being announced.
[F15] (exchange.v1 - 1.1) An exchange moves an existing booking to a different performance. It is not a refund followed by a repurchase, and the original booking reference is retained.
[F16] (exchange.v1 - 1.2) An exchange is a single operation across the whole booking. Individual tickets on one booking cannot be exchanged separately.
[F17] (exchange.v1 - 2.1) Exchanges are permitted up to 48 hours before the scheduled door time of the performance originally booked.
[F18] (exchange.v1 - 2.2) Where the performance being exchanged into has a higher ticket price, the difference is payable at the time of the exchange. Where it has a lower price, the difference is not refunded.
[F19] (exchange.v1 - 2.3) An exchange may be performed once per booking. A booking that has already been exchanged cannot be exchanged again.
[F20] (exchange.v1 - 3.1) A booking may only be exchanged into a performance with sufficient contiguous seating in the same price band as the original.
[F21] (exchange.v1 - 3.2) A booking whose tickets have been transferred to another named holder cannot be exchanged by the original purchaser.
[F22] (exchange.v1 - 3.3) Exchanges are unavailable for performances designated final-week by the promoter.
[F23] (exchange.v1 - 4.1) An exchange does not restart the refund window. The refund window of the original purchase continues to apply, measured against the original door time.
[F24] (exchange.v1 - 4.2) The booking fee is not recharged on an exchange.

# Established facts

### policy_clauses
[F1] (refund.v1 - 1.1) This policy governs refunds requested by the ticket holder. Refunds arising from an event being canceled or rescheduled by the promoter are governed by section 5 and are not subject to the windows in section 2.
[F2] (refund.v1 - 1.2) Every ticket is sold with a booking fee. The booking fee is stated separately at checkout.
[F3] (refund.v1 - 2.1) A full refund of the ticket price is available where the request is made more than 14 days before the scheduled door time.
[F4] (refund.v1 - 2.2) Where the request is made between 14 days and 72 hours before the scheduled door time, 50% of the ticket price is refundable.
[F5] (refund.v1 - 2.3) No refund of the ticket price is available where the request is made within 72 hours of the scheduled door time.
[F6] (refund.v1 - 2.4) The booking fee is non-refundable under this section, including where a full refund of the ticket price is due.
[F7] (refund.v1 - 3.1) A refund is issued to the original payment method. Where the original method is no longer valid, the refund is held until the account holder supplies a replacement.
[F8] (refund.v1 - 3.2) Card refunds are submitted to Cardinal Pay within one business day and reach the cardholder's statement within five business days of submission.
[F9] (refund.v1 - 3.3) Partial refunds against a split-tender payment are submitted to each instrument in the proportion originally charged.
[F10] (refund.v1 - 4.1) A refund cannot be issued against a booking whose tickets have been transferred to another named holder. The transfer must be reversed by the current holder before a refund can be requested.
[F11] (refund.v1 - 4.2) A booking that has been exchanged retains the refund window of the *original* purchase, not of the event it was exchanged into.
[F12] (refund.v1 - 4.3) Where any ticket on a booking has been scanned at the venue, no ticket on that booking is refundable.
[F13] (refund.v1 - 5.1) Where an event is canceled by the promoter, the ticket price and the booking fee are both refunded in full, automatically, within ten business days. No request is required.
[F14] (refund.v1 - 5.2) Where an event is rescheduled by the promoter, tickets remain valid for the new date. A holder who cannot attend the new date may request a full refund of the ticket price and the booking fee within 14 days of the reschedule being announced.

# Established facts

### policy_clauses
[F1] (refund.v1 - 1.1) This policy governs refunds requested by the ticket holder. Refunds arising from an event being canceled or rescheduled by the promoter are governed by section 5 and are not subject to the windows in section 2.
[F2] (refund.v1 - 1.2) Every ticket is sold with a booking fee. The booking fee is stated separately at checkout.
[F3] (refund.v1 - 2.1) A full refund of the ticket price is available where the request is made more than 14 days before the scheduled door time.
[F4] (refund.v1 - 2.2) Where the request is made between 14 days and 72 hours before the scheduled door time, 50% of the ticket price is refundable.
[F5] (refund.v1 - 2.3) No refund of the ticket price is available where the request is made within 72 hours of the scheduled door time.
[F6] (refund.v1 - 2.4) The booking fee is non-refundable under this section, including where a full refund of the ticket price is due.
[F7] (refund.v1 - 3.1) A refund is issued to the original payment method. Where the original method is no longer valid, the refund is held until the account holder supplies a replacement.
[F8] (refund.v1 - 3.2) Card refunds are submitted to Cardinal Pay within one business day and reach the cardholder's statement within five business days of submission.
[F9] (refund.v1 - 3.3) Partial refunds against a split-tender payment are submitted to each instrument in the proportion originally charged.
[F10] (refund.v1 - 4.1) A refund cannot be issued against a booking whose tickets have been transferred to another named holder. The transfer must be reversed by the current holder before a refund can be requested.
[F11] (refund.v1 - 4.2) A booking that has been exchanged retains the refund window of the *original* purchase, not of the event it was exchanged into.
[F12] (refund.v1 - 4.3) Where any ticket on a booking has been scanned at the venue, no ticket on that booking is refundable.
[F13] (refund.v1 - 5.1) Where an event is canceled by the promoter, the ticket price and the booking fee are both refunded in full, automatically, within ten business days. No request is required.
[F14] (refund.v1 - 5.2) Where an event is rescheduled by the promoter, tickets remain valid for the new date. A holder who cannot attend the new date may request a full refund of the ticket price and the booking fee within 14 days of the reschedule being announced.

[F12] (refund.v1 - 4.3) Where any ticket on a booking has been scanned at the venue, no ticket on that booking is refundable.
[F13] (refund.v1 - 5.1) Where an event is canceled by the promoter, the ticket price and the booking fee are both refunded in full, automatically, within ten business days. No request is required.
[F14] (refund.v1 - 5.2) Where an event is rescheduled by the promoter, tickets remain valid for the new date. A holder who cannot attend the new date may request a full refund of the ticket price and the booking fee within 14 days of the reschedule being announced.

# Established facts

### policy_clauses
[F1] (refund.v1 - 1.1) This policy governs refunds requested by the ticket holder. Refunds arising from an event being canceled or rescheduled by the promoter are governed by section 5 and are not subject to the windows in section 2.
[F2] (refund.v1 - 1.2) Every ticket is sold with a booking fee. The booking fee is stated separately at checkout.
[F3] (refund.v1 - 2.1) A full refund of the ticket price is available where the request is made more than 14 days before the scheduled door time.
[F4] (refund.v1 - 2.2) Where the request is made between 14 days and 72 hours before the scheduled door time, 50% of the ticket price is refundable.
[F5] (refund.v1 - 2.3) No refund of the ticket price is available where the request is made within 72 hours of the scheduled door time.
[F6] (refund.v1 - 2.4) The booking fee is non-refundable under this section, including where a full refund of the ticket price is due.
[F7] (refund.v1 - 3.1) A refund is issued to the original payment method. Where the original method is no longer valid, the refund is held until the account holder supplies a replacement.
[F8] (refund.v1 - 3.2) Card refunds are submitted to Cardinal Pay within one business day and reach the cardholder's statement within five business days of submission.
[F9] (refund.v1 - 3.3) Partial refunds against a split-tender payment are submitted to each instrument in the proportion originally charged.
[F10] (refund.v1 - 4.1) A refund cannot be issued against a booking whose tickets have been transferred to another named holder. The transfer must be reversed by the current holder before a refund can be requested.
[F11] (refund.v1 - 4.2) A booking that has been exchanged retains the refund window of the *original* purchase, not of the event it was exchanged into.
[F12] (refund.v1 - 4.3) Where any ticket on a booking has been scanned at the venue, no ticket on that booking is refundable.
[F13] (refund.v1 - 5.1) Where an event is canceled by the promoter, the ticket price and the booking fee are both refunded in full, automatically, within ten business days. No request is required.
[F14] (refund.v1 - 5.2) Where an event is rescheduled by the promoter, tickets remain valid for the new date. A holder who cannot attend the new date may request a full refund of the ticket price and the booking fee within 14 days of the reschedule being announced.
